_**The Reality War**_ is coming. After weeks of cryptic dialogue and teasing glimpses, **_[Doctor Who](https://poppednews.com/doctor-who/)_** has finally pulled back the curtain on one of its most mysterious new figures — and the twist is bigger than anyone expected. In a dramatic reveal during **_[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/17/doctor-who-season-2-the-interstellar-song-contest-review/)_**, **Anita Dobson’s** enigmatic Mrs Flood was unveiled as none other than the Rani — a classic villain from the show’s storied past, now reimagined in a bi-generated twist that introduces Emmy Award-winner **Archie Panjabi** into the mix. In the first part of the _Doctor Who_ Season 2 finale, titled **_Wish World_**, releasing this week, traps are sprung and old enemies unite as the Doctor (**Ncuti Gatwa**) and Belinda (**Varada Sethu**) finally arrive home to find a very different world. Can the Doctor see the truth before midnight arrives? Following on from an inevitable cliffhanger, the final part, titled _The Reality War,_ will conclude the season, tying up loose ends – but what is the synopsis and who will appear?

![Image 1: tbTwYCVI o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/tbTwYCVI_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The **[official BBC synopsis](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002d3lr)** for the _Doctor Who_ Season 2 finale, titled “The Reality War” reads:

> _Battle rages across the skies as the Unholy Trinity unleash their deadly ambition. The Doctor, Belinda and Ruby have to risk everything in the quest to save one innocent life._

_The Reality War_ is currently listed as having a **66 minute runtime**.

‘Doctor Who’ Season 2: “The Reality War” Cast List
--------------------------------------------------

![Image 2: 0hHdj1TV o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/0hHdj1TV_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The Doctor, portrayed by **Ncuti Gatwa**, leads the charge in this climactic episode. He is joined by his companions: Belinda Chandra, played by **Varada Sethu**, and Ruby Sunday, portrayed by **Millie Gibson**.

Key supporting characters include The Unholy Trinity, comprised of **Mrs. Flood**, whose true identity as the Rani was recently revealed, played by **Anita Dobson**. Joining her side is the recently bi-generated The Rani, played by **Archie Panjabi**, and **[Conrad Clark](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/03/doctor-who-season-2-lucky-day-review/)**, Ruby’s former boyfriend turned antagonist, is portrayed by **Jonah Hauer-King**.

UNIT personnel make significant appearances: The Vlinx, voiced by **Nicholas Briggs**, Kate Lethbridge-Stewart is played by **Jemma Redgrave**, Shirley Bingham by **Ruth Madeley**, and Colonel Christofer Ibrahim by **Alexander Devrient**. Rose Noble returns, played by **Yasmin Finney** and other notable characters include Melanie Bush, portrayed by **Bonnie Langford**, and Susan Triad, played by **Susan Twist**.

![Image 3: wSyFB7Pw o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/wSyFB7Pw_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

![Image 4: 2Hpp3gyO o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2Hpp3gyO_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

Additional cast members include Poppy, played by **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps**, who makes her third appearance since first debuting in last season’s opener **_[Space Babies](https://poppednews.com/2024/05/06/doctor-who-season-1-premiere-review/)_**. Ruby’s family members, Carla Sunday and Cherry Sunday, are portrayed by **Michelle Greenidge** and **Angela Wynter**, respectively. **Sam Lawton** and **Nila Aalia** appear elsewhere as Winnie Petheridge and Lakshmi Chandra, respectively.

Where Can I Watch “The Reality War”?
------------------------------------

![Image 5: Varada Sethu, Ncuti Gatwa and Millie Gibson at a table read for 'Doctor Who' Season 2.](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Ncuti-Millie-Varada-2-6762aed.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The episode will premiere on **Saturday, May 31st 2025**, during a primetime evening slot of **6:50 pm** on **BBC One**. It will also be available to stream on **BBC iPlayer** at the same time. Unlike earlier episodes this season, **[_“The Reality War”_ will not have an early morning iPlayer release](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/12/doctor-who-season-2-the-reality-war-simultaneous-premiere/)**; instead, it will debut simultaneously with the TV broadcast to ensure a unified viewing experience

For a cinematic experience, over **450 cinemas across the UK and Ireland** will host special screenings of the two-part finale, featuring both _Wish World_ and _The Reality War_, on **May 31**. Tickets can be booked through the official site: [**doctorwhoincinemas.co.uk**](https://www.doctorwhoincinemas.co.uk/).

Outside the UK, _The Reality War_ will be available on **[Disney+](http://disneyplus.com/)** in regions where the service is accessible. The episode will stream simultaneously with the UK broadcast, ensuring fans worldwide can watch together.[](https://cultbox.co.uk/news/episodes-news/doctor-who-finale-will-transmit-simultaneously-worldwide-at-7pm-bt?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

* * *

The first part of the finale, _Wish World_, arrives on **Saturday, May 24,** exclusively on BBC iPlayer from 8am and Disney+ internationally. The concluding episode, _**[The Reality War](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/12/doctor-who-season-2-the-reality-war-simultaneous-premiere/)**_, will premiere with a cinematic flourish on **Saturday, May** **31**, debuting simultaneously on BBC One, BBC iPlayer, and in **over 450 cinemas** across the UK and Ireland.

6.content:
“Timey wimey” doesn’t even begin to describe the Season 2 finale of _Doctor Who_. “The Reality War” brought the season’s long-running mystery — the Earth mysteriously being destroyed suddenly on May 24, 2025 — to its conclusion, but introduced a last-minute twist that saw the end of Ncuti Gatwa’s 15th Doctor, and the return of a _very_ familiar face. But what does it all mean? Is the 15th Doctor really gone? Is the 16th Doctor really who she seems to be? Let’s dig into the wild, twisty ending of “The Reality War.”

**Spoilers ahead for _Doctor Who_’s “The Reality War.”**

Doctor Who “The Reality War” Ending Explained
---------------------------------------------

The crux of the episode’s late climax, and the reason for the 15th Doctor’s regeneration, is the existence of Poppy.

BBC

“The Reality War” picks up with “Wish World’s” very literal cliffhanger by having the Doctor saved from his fall by Anita (Steph de Whalley), the hotel receptionist with whom the Doctor spent a whole year during the [2024 Christmas special](https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/doctor-who-paradox-joy-to-the-world-big-bang). But Anita’s gotten a promotion to be the manager of the Time Hotel, which gives her access to a key that can open a door to any time. The time of May 24, 2025, however, is causing the Time Hotel to spasm, as the fate of Earth on this day puts the Hotel and its entire structure at risk of collapse. With Anita’s help, the Doctor breaks UNIT out of their Wish World-induced haze, and brings Belinda and their daughter Poppy back to the UNIT headquarters to wage war against [the Rani](https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/who-is-the-rani-mrs-flood-archie-panjabi-doctor-who) (Archie Panjabi), Mrs. Flood aka also the Rani (Anita Dobson), and Conrad (Jonah Hauer-King).

The Rani’s plan, it turns out, is to bring Omega back to create a new Gallifrey — and she needs him to create the blueprint for a new Time Lord race, as the Master’s destruction of Gallifrey and genocide of its people left the surviving Time Lords (aka the Rani and the Doctor) infertile. Though the existence of Poppy throws a wrench in this whole explanation and scheme, the Doctor points out, as she shouldn’t be able to be created from his DNA. But she is real, and he and Belinda (Varada Sethu) are determined to make sure she will exist after the Wish World is destroyed, with the Doctor tasking Susan Triad (Susan Twist) with building a Zero Room in which Belinda and Poppy can be kept safe from the disintegrating reality.

And when the Rani and Omega are defeated by the Doctor (at alarming speed, thanks to a giant, zombified Omega eating Rani and the Doctor’s conveniently-placed Vindicator), their plan seems to have worked: they open the Zero Room, and out steps Belinda with a still-real Poppy. But when the Doctor returns with Belinda, Poppy, and Ruby (Millie Gibson) to the TARDIS, Ruby notices something odd happen: Poppy disappears, and the Doctor and Belinda don’t seem to remember her. When she tearfully pleads with the Doctor to save Poppy — who appears to have been a victim of “time shifting by one degree” — the Doctor jumps into the TARDIS with plans to use his regeneration energy to punch a hole into the time vortex and shift reality into its proper place. That’s when the first familiar face pops up.

Jodie Whittaker makes a brief cameo as the 13th Doctor, to warn the 15th Doctor about the dangers of punching a hole in the time vortex.

BBC

Jodie Whittaker’s 13th Doctor appears in the TARDIS, thanks to a “schism in time” caused by reality snapping back in place after the disintegration of the Wish World. She warns the 15th Doctor not to use his regeneration energy, as it could destroy the time vortex and all of reality — but concedes quickly as he tells her of the life at stake. (Side note: Whittaker has never been better than in these brief minutes written by Russell T Davies, one wishes her dialogue was as good as this in her era.) She heads off to _not_ confess her love to Yaz, and the 15th Doctor prepares to blow a hole in the time vortex.

Suddenly, he wakes in the backyard of Belinda’s home and learns that Poppy is not his daughter, but only Belinda’s — a few inserted scenes of Belinda talking about Poppy throughout their adventures reveal that she had a daughter all along — and that’s why she was so desperate to get home. Happy that Belinda is reunited with the daughter she was desperate to return to, the Doctor heads off to finish his regeneration... and that’s when the biggest twist of the episode happens.

Billie Piper as the 16th Doctor?
--------------------------------

The 15th Doctor regenerates at the end of this episode, with his face bursting into light and turning into... Billie Piper’s. “Oh, hello!” she says as she recognizes her new face.

That’s right, the actress who played the 9th (Christopher Eccleston) and 10th Doctor’s (David Tennant) companion, Rose Tyler, is back but as the Doctor. And yes, that means that Ncuti Gatwa’s 15th Doctor is gone: Gatwa confirms in this behind-the-scenes [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dz-35CJcgCc) that his [era as the Doctor is over](https://www.doctorwho.tv/news-and-features/ncuti-gatwa-says-final-farewell-to-the-tardis-as-the-fifteenth-doctor-regenerates). It feels like a shame that his era ends after two seasons (making his run as the Doctor one of the shortest in the history of the show), especially after the 15th Doctor finally felt like he was [coming into his own with Season 2](https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/doctor-who-season-2-review-bbc-disney-plus). But we’re given little time to grieve his departure, with the reveal of the next Doctor — or is she?

Billie Piper as Rose Tyler_._

BBC

But is Billie Piper really the 16th Doctor? Tinfoil hat theory time: In the credits, we see “Introducing Billie Piper,” but notably _not “_as the Doctor.” Could there still be ripple effects left from the reality shift caused by the disintegration of the Wish World? Is this another “glitch,” as UNIT calls the handful of other discrepancies? Or maybe she’s playing “Bad Wolf,” as she did in the 50th anniversary special, “The Day of the Doctor”? And does this mean Russell T Davies is building up to a very awkward reunion between Tennant’s 14th Doctor and Piper’s Doctor?

Who knows if we will find out soon, as [_Doctor Who_’s future on Disney+ remains unknown](https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/doctor-who-new-showrunner-rumor). The only thing confirmed to be coming next in the Whoniverse in the [_The War Between the Land and the Sea_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoM7pfpE3u0) [spinoff](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoM7pfpE3u0), but it’s clear that the main show is building up to something big again. Or maybe it’s just another [nostalgia ploy to keep the show afloat](https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/doctor-who-review-the-star-beast-60th-anniversary-special). At the very least, _Doctor Who_ does what it does best: it leaves us bewildered, and oddly emotional, but always wanting more.

#### _Doctor Who_ streams on Disney+ and HBO Max. Classic episodes of the show can be found on Tubi.

Doctor Who 2.8 Review: The Reality War
--------------------------------------

The Doctor and Belinda race to save their daughter as Omega is unleashed…

[Pete Messum](https://criticalpopcorn.com/author/thepetemessum/)

Jun 1, 2025

5–8 minutes

[Alex Sanjiv Pillai](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/alex-sanjiv-pillai/), [Anita Dobson](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/anita-dobson/), [Archie Panjabi](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/archie-panjabi/), [BBC](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/bbc/), [BBC Doctor Who](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/bbc-doctor-who/), [BBC iPlayer](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/bbc-iplayer/), [BBC One](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/bbc-one/), [Billie Piper](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/billie-piper/), [Disney](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/disney/), [Doctor Who](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who/), [Doctor Who 15](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-15/), [Doctor Who 2025](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-2025/), [Doctor Who Disney+](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-disney/), [Doctor Who Series 15](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-series-15/), [Doctor Who Series Blog](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-series-blog/), [Doctor Who The Reality War](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-the-reality-war/), [Doctor Who Wish World](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-wish-world/), [Doctor Who: Season 2](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-season-2/), [Jodie Whittaker](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/jodie-whittaker/), [Ncuti Gatwa](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/ncuti-gatwa/), [Russell T Davies](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/russell-t-davies/), [Ruth Madeley](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/ruth-madeley/), [science fiction](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/science-fiction/), [Streaming](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/streaming/), [The Reality War](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/the-reality-war/), [TV](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/tv/), [Varada Sethu](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/varada-sethu/), [Whoniverse](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/whoniverse/), [Wish World](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/wish-world/), [Yasmin Finney](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/yasmin-finney/)

It was difficult not to feel trepidatious heading into _**[Doctor Who](https://criticalpopcorn.com/tag/doctor-who-series-blog/)**_’s season 2 finale. Last year’s _**[Empire of Death](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2024/06/23/doctor-who-1-8-review-empire-of-death/)**_ ended the Fifteenth Doctor’s first season on a disappointing note: a perfectly watchable final episode that didn’t resolve the season-long mysteries in a particularly satisfying way (even if it’s easy to see why certain creative choices were made). _**The Reality War**_, on the other hand, is a complete mess of an episode from start to finish. There’s clearly an attempt to bring the entirety of this era of **_Doctor Who_** together like in Series 4’s finale _**The Stolen Earth**_ and **_Journey’s End_**, but it all feels like a last-minute scramble to resolve a 21-episode run that’s primarily suffered from overblown stakes, an overabundance of gratuitous fan service and a distinct lack of character development.

[![Image 2](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/doctor-who-2025-the-reality-war-ncuti-gatwa-regenerates-fifteenth-doctor.png?w=1024)](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/doctor-who-2025-the-reality-war-ncuti-gatwa-regenerates-fifteenth-doctor.png)

Opening the episode with a call-back to _**[Joy to the World](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2024/12/26/doctor-who-joy-to-the-world-review-2024-christmas-special/)**_ – the most recent Christmas Special, and the up until now the worst episode of this era by far – certainly started things in an odd place. In a way, it’s good to see that the Time Hotel hasn’t been entirely forgotten about, and in a timey-wimey way it does make sense that it can help reality reassert itself at U.N.I.T Tower, but then everything stops dead. Director **Alex Sanjiv Pillai** leaves virtually the entire cast standing still for about five minutes so that the Doctor and the Rani can talk _at_ each other, throwing out references to _**Time and the Rani**_, bizarre lore changes (apparently Time Lords are infertile now) and clunky exposition. **Bonnie Langford**’s Mel meeting the Rani again (albeit now played by a wasted **Archie Panjabi**) seems ripe for some interesting character development, but that’s immediately squandered. The Rani wanting to start a new race of Time Lords is an interesting idea left half-baked. After hanging around for two whole seasons, **Anita Dobson**’s Rani is still pushed aside and left as a dangling thread for future episodes. **Yasmin Finney** returns as Rose only to stand around with nothing to do…just like in last year’s season finale. It’s difficult not to feel that Finney has been wasted in a role that seemed on paper like a new great recurring character. Shirley’s rebellion against Conrad set up last week is retconned out of existence, but at least **Ruth Madeley** gets to fire lasers at the giant bone beasts, so she’s not completely wasted here.

This two-parter as a whole is filled with wasted potential. The concept of the Wish World could probably sustain an entire eight-episode season of _**Doctor Who**_ and develop in interesting ways that fully explore the concept and the characters living through it, but it’s rushed through by the time **_The Reality War_** even gets going. The Doctor having a daughter in Poppy is an idea filled with dramatic potential but the whole thread feels like hollow emotional stakes that haven’t been earned. Omega returning should feel like a big deal – he’s the Time Lord who gave the Time Lords time travel, and he’s trapped in another universe – but he’s left as a giant lumbering corpse, not dissimilar to the huge Sutekh dog last season. Even a human-sized corpse would be more creepy and threatening. It’s fair to say that these classic villains always need some kind of reinterpretation in the 21st century, but the way that **Russell T Davies** has handled Sutekh, the Rani and Omega is incredibly frustrating. These are villains with so much dramatic potential but Davies refuses to explore any of this.

[![Image 3](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/doctor-who-2025-the-reality-war-vlinx.png?w=1024)](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/doctor-who-2025-the-reality-war-vlinx.png)

_**The Reality War**_ rushes through so much that it’s a bit of a whiplash when it screeches to a halt to end on **Ncuti Gatwa**’s regeneration sequence. It had been rumoured for months, but the moment of realisation — that the Fifteenth Doctor’s in the TARDIS had already come to an abrupt end — was genuinely so disappointing. Whatever the reasons were behind the scenes for his departure (this evidently wasn’t the plan, given how much of the ending appears to be last-minute reshoots), to have the Fifteenth Doctor depart after only 19 episodes with no sense of resolution to his journey as a character is a real shame. Gatwa’s run on the series may not be the shortest, but it already feels like one littered with wasted potential. His reunion with his granddaughter Susan, set up back in **_[The Devil’s Chord](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2024/05/12/doctor-who-1-2-review-the-devils-chord/)_** and reiterated in the last two episodes, is left unresolved. The Fifteenth Doctor will never find Rogue in the Hell Dimension. And, unlike almost all of his predecessors, he didn’t even fight his greatest enemies, the Daleks. **Ncuti Gatwa** was such an exciting choice for the Fifteenth Doctor, and it’s clear that he’s thrown so much into his performance over the last two seasons that it will be difficult not to miss him in the role.

And, if _**Doctor Who: Unleashed**_ is anything to go by, this is the last time we’ll be seeing companions Ruby Sunday and Belinda Chandra. Despite her strong performance in **_[Lucky Day](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2025/05/04/doctor-who-2-4-review-lucky-day/)_**, **Millie Gibson** was wasted in this two-part finale, and her final scene didn’t even register as one on a first viewing. It was difficult not to assume that she’d have a larger role in this season finale but like with most of the cast she seemed to just stand around waiting for something to do. **Varada Sethu** is as excellent as ever in _**The Reality War**_ but despite the strong introduction to Belinda in **_[The Robot Revolution](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2025/04/13/doctor-who-2-1-review-the-robot-revolution/)_**, the character has been pushed aside for most of this season, relegated to a generic companion role. It’s probably fair to say that the Fifteenth Doctor has had good companions, but both of them needed more screentime to develop into all-time great companions.

On a positive note, it was lovely to see **Jodie Whittaker** cameo as the Thirteenth Doctor, bringing her familiar energy and enthusiasm for the role in a pre-regeneration scene which strangely didn’t feel too out-of-place, even if it may have done so on paper. To have the Doctor’s predecessor support them in a regeneration is a nice idea, and it’s always good to see Whittaker don her rainbow-striped-top. Credit also has to be given to the VFX artists for going all-in on such a bonkers sequence as the U.N.I.T Tower battling the bone beasts as the Doctor skis into the Rani’s bone palace, _**[Flash Gordon](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2020/07/30/flash-gordon-40th-anniversary-blu-ray-review-dir-mike-hodges/)**_ style.

![Image 4](https://images2.imgbox.com/00/ae/9fzuq4Dm_o.jpg)

It’s probably too early to determine exactly _how_ disappointing _**The Reality War**_ is – as a finale to Season 2, as the Fifteenth Doctor’s last adventure, or as the last of this era of _**Doctor Who**_ (although we’ll have to wait and see on the latter) – but there’s no denying that this was a spectacular letdown on almost every level. It’s not a complete trainwreck: the cast are game, and as with any **Russell T Davies** story, there are some strong moments sprinkled throughout, but the script overall is a mess, and most surprisingly, directed in a pretty lacklustre manner. Some episodes grow on us over time (_**[The Giggle](https://criticalpopcorn.com/2023/12/10/doctor-who-the-giggle-review-60th-anniversary-special/)**_ is more satisfying on a rewatch than on first viewing, for instance), while others don’t hold up particularly well. Perhaps _**The Reality War**_ will shift into the former category, but as it stands, it’s a disappointing end to a mixed bag of a season.

As for the future of _**Doctor Who**_? Time will tell. It always does.

[![Image 5](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/2000px-2_stars-svg.png?w=1024)](https://criticalpopcorn.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/2000px-2_stars-svg.png)

**_Doctor Who_ will return**
============================

### Written by Russell T Davies _"This has been an absolute joy..."_
Episode TitlePremiere Date
The Reality War31/05/2025
Battle rages across the skies as the Unholy Trinity unleash their deadly ambition. The Doctor, Belinda and Ruby have to risk everything, in the quest to save one innocent life. Turn on Javascript to see all the available pictures * * * ### Plot As [the Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/fifteenth-doctor) plummets into the Underverse, he is saved by the timely appearance of his friend, Time Hotel manager [Anita Benn](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/anita-benn). Escaping through a doorway into the time-travelling holiday destination, Anita explains that the hotel is becoming unstable due to the Rani’s constant repetition of May 23rd, 2025. With real time restoring his memories fully, the Doctor and Anita return to the Wish World to ensure the safety of [Belinda](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/belinda-chandra) and [Poppy](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/poppy). While [the Rani](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-rani) and [Mrs Flood](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/mrs-flood) prepare the final stage of their plan to find [Omega](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/omega), the Doctor and Anita bring the Time Hotel doors to UNIT Tower; where the flow of real time restores the memories of [Kate Lethbridge-Stewart](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/kate-lethbridge-stewart), [Colonel Ibrahim](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/colonel-christofer-ibrahim), and everyone else on duty. Kate wakes up [Ruby Sunday](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/ruby-sunday), [Shirley Bingham](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/shirley-bingham) and [Mel Bush](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/mel-bush) using their UNIT bio-chips. As the team assembles, the Rani confronts the Doctor in UNIT HQ, where she reveals her plan is to use Omega’s body as a gene bank to begin a new race of Time Lords. The Doctor insists that Poppy’s existence is proof that there is another way to achieve her goals without need of the Mad God. Returning to the Bone Palace, the Rani sets the [Bone Beasts](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/bone-beasts) on UNIT Tower to prevent them from interfering in her plan, as UNIT Tower becomes an active battle station in response to the threat. As battle rages, the Doctor and [Susan Triad](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/susan-triad) build a Zero Room to protect Poppy from the effects of [Conrad Clark](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/conrad-clark)’s wish. Determined to protect her daughter, Belinda enters the Zero Room with Poppy. The Doctor and Ruby both make their way to the Bone Palace to confront the Rani and Conrad respectively. The Doctor arrives just as the Rani executes her final plan, opening a doorway for Omega to enter from the Underverse. The original Time Lord emerges – now a hulking, decaying titan. Declaring himself as a God of Time, Omega snatches up the Rani and eats her whole. As Mrs Flood makes her escape using the Rani’s Time Ring, the Doctor is left to face the Mad God alone. Grabbing the stolen Vindicator, the Doctor blasts Omega with a powerful beam that drives him back into the Underverse, ending the titan’s threat. Using an Indigo Device, Ruby teleports to Conrad to face her ex-boyfriend once more. Failing to appeal to his better nature, Ruby tricks Conrad by teleporting behind him and grabbing the baby [Desiderium](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/desiderium). She makes her own wish for Conrad to be happy and he disappears. As Ruby ends the wish that created this reality, she finds herself and the baby inside the Doctor’s [TARDIS](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-tardis). Returning to UNIT, the Doctor is delighted to find that both Belinda and Poppy emerge from the Zero Room unscathed. Not knowing where Desiderium came from, the Doctor and Ruby bring the baby to [Carla](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/carla-sunday) and [Cherry Sunday](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/cherry-sunday); who take the child in as one of their own, naming the child Joseph Sunday. Bringing Poppy to the TARDIS, the Doctor and Belinda plan where they want to go next – but Poppy disappears as they speak, leaving Ruby as the only person who can remember her. At UNIT, the TARDIS team discover that since the end of the wish, there are a few permanent changes to reality – and Conrad Clark is alive and well, with no memory or record of who he was before. Ruby pleads to the Doctor to remember and find Poppy, who she believes is lost in the cracks of time. Determined not to lose an innocent life, the Doctor leaves his companions behind and departs in the TARDIS. Knowing his next action will cost him his life, the Doctor prepares to sacrifice himself; but is suddenly interrupted by one of his predecessors, the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/thirteenth-doctor)! She has appeared in the TARDIS as a result of a “giant time schism” that the Doctor is about to cause. Unable to talk him out of his plan, the Doctor offers her future self some words of wisdom and comfort before returning to her own time. The Doctor then triggers a release of his regeneration energy and targets it on the TARDIS console, creating the schism in the Time Vortex. The Doctor wakes up in a garden, where he is reunited with Belinda and to his delight, Poppy. Time has re-aligned itself, Poppy has survived and remains Belinda’s daughter - however, she now has a human father instead of the Doctor. Belinda reminds "Uncle Doctor" that she was _always_ trying to get back to May 24th at 7:30am, to pick up Poppy. Satisfied that they are both safe and happy, the Doctor bids both Belinda and Poppy farewell. Seeking company, the Doctor takes the TARDIS in view of the star that was once his friend, [Joy Almondo](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/joy-almondo). Reflecting on the "absolute joy" of his most recent life, the Doctor embraces the regeneration that will carry him into the next... ### Featuring * * * ### Concept Art Turn on Javascript to see all the available pictures * * * ### Behind the Scenes * Jodie Whittaker appears as the Thirteenth Doctor for the first time since her final episode [_The Power of the Doctor_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-power-of-the-doctor). Her inclusion in the story was so top-secret that she was given the codename “Petrol” in both the script and shooting call sheet. * Anita’s sequence of searching for the Doctor in the Time Hotel uses footage of Matt Smith’s [Eleventh Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/eleventh-doctor) in [_The Wedding of River Song_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-wedding-of-river-song) and Jon Pertwee’s [Third Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/third-doctor) in [_Day of the Daleks_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/day-of-the-daleks). A real scene-accurate [Dalek](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/daleks) was used on the day of shooting, at director Alex Sanjiv Pillai's request.

#### Synopsis

From Book 1:

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan runs a small business out of a Tudor cottage in the sleepy English village of Elstow. But Radlan was born in 2951, and when he falls in love with a local girl, he has to choose between running from his own people and condemning his lover to die.  
  
He makes the wrong choice.  
  
Travelling into the past, falling in love... it turns out he was _meant_ to do these things. He's been manipulated all along, but now he's slipped his handlers, and Time is no longer following the right script. Other versions of history vie for dominance, and our reality is losing.

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan sparked **The Reality War**.

_The Reality War_ is a two-novel series that echoes _The Pilgrim's Progress_ by John Bunyan. It is both a sci-fi action-adventure series, and a spiritual journey made by two people, mirror images of each other from rival realities. It is a side story set in the bestselling Human Legion Universe (Human Legion, Sleeping Legion, Revenge Squad, Chimera Company).

7.content:
Following the dramatic cliffhanger to Wish World, this week sees the 15th season of [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) come to a close in epic style, with an episode titled The Reality War.

According to the episode's synopsis, it will see battle rage across the skies as the Unholy Trinity unleash their deadly ambition. Meanwhile, the Doctor, Belinda and Ruby have to risk everything in their quest to save one innocent life.

Of course, Ncuti Gatwa, Varada Sethu and Millie Gibson are all back, as are Archie Panjabi, Anita Dobson and Jonah Hauer-King who play the episode's central villains. But who else will we see back for the finale and who do they all play?

Read on for everything you need to know about the cast of Doctor Who season 15 episode 8, The Reality War.

**Who's in the cast of Doctor Who: The Reality War? Full list of characters in season 15 episode 8**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The main cast for Doctor Who: The Reality War is as follows. Scroll on to find out more about the characters, plus where you may have seen the actors previously.

*   **Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor**
*   **Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra**
*   **Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday**
*   **Archie Panjabi as The Rani**
*   **Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood**
*   **Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark**
*   **Sam Lawton as Winnie Petheridge**
*   **Ruth Madeley as Shirley Bingham**
*   **Michelle Gr****eenidge as Carla Sunday**
*   **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy**
*   **Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart**
*   **Susan Twist as Susan Triad**
*   **Alexander Devrient as Colonel Christopher Ibrahim**
*   **Aidan Cook as The Vlinx**
*   **Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble**
*   **Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush**
*   **Angela Wynter as Cherry Sunday**
*   **Nila Aalia as Lakshmi Chandra**

**Ncuti Gatwa plays The Doctor**
--------------------------------

![Image 1: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who, wearing a blue suit, leaning on a table and looking at the camera](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/517536-b556059.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is the Doctor?** The Doctor is a time traveller from Gallifrey, and the last of the Time Lords. He travels in space and time in the TARDIS. This version of the character is known as the Fifteenth Doctor, although we know there have been a number of additional incarnations.

**Where have I seen Ncuti Gatwa before?** Beyond his role as the Doctor, Gatwa is best known for his role as Eric Effiong in Sex Education, as well as for starring in [Barbie](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/barbie-review/) and [Masters of the Air](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/masters-of-the-air-release-date/).

**Varada Sethu plays Belinda Chandra**
--------------------------------------

![Image 2: Varada Sethu as her character in Doctor Who, looking concerned under dramatic lighting, wearing a white ribbed top with a collar and subtle jewellery, with blurred studio lights glowing in the background.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521378-c6f8a66.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is Belinda Chandra?** Belinda is a nurse from London who, in The Robot Revolution, was kidnapped by robots and flown to the stars on their rocket.

At the end of the episode, she told the Doctor to take her home in the TARDIS, but he found himself unable to get back to that particular date, time and location. In The Interstellar Song Contest, they found out this was because the Earth was destroyed on that date. In Wish World, she believed she was married to the Doctor, who was known as John Smith, and that Poppy was their daughter.

**Where have I seen Varada Sethu before?** Sethu is no stranger to Doctor Who, having played Mundy Flynn in last season's episode 3, [Boom](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-varada-sethu-nods-boom-character-exclusive-newsupdate/). She is also known for her roles in series such as [Andor](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/andor-season-3-explained/), Strike Back, Doctor Foster, Hard Sun and [Annika](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/nicola-walker-annika-fourth-wall-comment/), as well as films including Now You See Me 2, [Jurassic World: Dominion](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/scifi/jurassic-world-rebirth-release-date/) and I Came By.

**Millie Gibson plays Ruby Sunday**
-----------------------------------

![Image 3: Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who episode Wish World. She's wearing a red top and denim jacket, with her face lit by the sun, looking into the distance](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520876-0f56101.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Ruby Sunday?** Ruby is the Doctor's former companion, who left the TARDIS to return to her old life after the Doctor helped her find her birth mother. In Wish World, she was seen joining Shirley, Winnie and their team to rebel against Conrad, as she had more access to her old memories than most.

**Where have I seen Millie Gibson before?** Outside of her role in Doctor Who, Gibson is best known for playing Kelly in [Coronation Street](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/coronation-street/), while she has also appeared in Jamie Johnson and Butterfly.

**Archie Panjabi plays The Rani**
---------------------------------

![Image 4: Archie Panjabi as the Rani in Doctor Who. She stands in a rustic wooden cabin, lit by shafts of moody natural light. Wearing a deep red Victorian-style dress under a dark cape, she stares intensely at the camera, flanked by hanging tools and animal pelts.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520878-1550a15.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Archie Panjabi as the Rani in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is the Rani?** In The Interstellar Song Contest, Mrs Flood bi-generated, splitting into two incarnations of the same Time Lady – the second, played by Archie Panjabi, declares herself "The Rani – the definite article".

The Rani is no stranger to long-time Doctor Who fans. A renegade Time Lord and amoral biochemist, she first appeared in the 1980s, portrayed by Kate O'Mara. Known for her ruthless scientific pursuits and disregard for ethical boundaries, The Rani clashed with both the Doctor and the Master in classic stories such as [The Mark of the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-guide/the-mark-of-the-rani/) and [Time and the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-guide/time-and-the-rani/). Her last on-screen appearance came in 1993’s charity special Dimensions in Time, but she’s remained a fan favourite, resurfacing in audio dramas and novels, with Siobhan Redmond taking on the role in Big Finish productions.

In Wish World, she was seen using the God of Wishes to create a false reality from the mind of Conrad Clark. Her plan was always to make the Doctor doubt the reality, causing into crumble and open up the Underverse, where she hopes to find Omega.

**Where have I seen Archie Panjabi before?** Panjabi is best known for her Emmy-winning role as Kalinda Sharma in the US TV drama The Good Wife.

Panjabi made early impressions in British films such as East Is East and Bend It Like Beckham, and later gained international recognition for her powerful performances in both television and film. She became the first Asian actor to win a Primetime Emmy Award for acting, earning widespread acclaim for her portrayal of the enigmatic Kalinda.

Beyond The Good Wife, Panjabi has appeared in shows including The Fall, Blindspot, Departure and [Hijack](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/hijack-season-2-apple-tv-release-date/), as well as films like A Mighty Heart.

**Anita Dobson plays Mrs Flood**
--------------------------------

![Image 5: Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who in a black and white outfit](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/523236-cceed68.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Mrs Flood?** As revealed in The Interstellar Song Contest, Mrs Flood is an incarnation of the Doctor’s old nemesis and Time Lady, [the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-the-rani-explained/). Ever since The Church on Ruby Road, she has appeared as a mysterious figure, even posing as the next-door neighbour of the Doctor's companions, Ruby Sunday and Belinda Chandra.

She has a habit of speaking directly to the camera and has made many threatening assertions towards the Doctor, although he is yet to become aware of her. In The Interstellar Song Contest, she bi-generated, and is now a subordinate to her next incarnation.

**Where have I seen Anita Dobson before?** Dobson is best known for playing Angie Watts in [EastEnders](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/), while she has also appeared in series including Casualty, [Call the Midwife](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/call-the-midwife-season-15-release-date/), Dodger and [Inside No. 9](https://www.radiotimes.com/going-out/going-out-reviews/inside-no-9-stage-fright-review/), and took part in [Strictly Come Dancing](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/entertainment/strictly-come-dancing-confirms-2025-professionals-newsupdate/) in 2011.

**Jonah Hauer-King plays Conrad Clark**
---------------------------------------

![Image 6: Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark in Doctor Who episode Wish World](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520867-4e355d3.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark in Doctor Who episode Wish World. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Conrad Clark?** Conrad is the leader of Think Tank, a group he used to amplify dangerous conspiracy theories about UNIT for financial gain. He previously posed as an alien-obsessed podcaster and struck up a romance with Ruby Sunday to trick her. At the end of Lucky Day, he was freed by Mrs Flood, and is now in league with her and The Rani, creating 'Wish World'.

**Where have I seen Jonah Hauer-King before?** Hauer-King is known for his roles in series including World on Fire, The Flatshare and [The Tattooist of Auschwitz](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/tattooist-of-auschwitz-release-date/), as well as films such as A Dog's Way Home, The Little Mermaid and [William Tell](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/william-tell-review-historical-epic/).

**Sam Lawton plays Winnie Petheridge**
--------------------------------------

![Image 7: Ruth Madeley as Shirley and Sam Lawton as Winnie](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521371-5378229.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ruth Madeley as Shirley and Sam Lawton as Winnie. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Samuel Dore

**Who is Winnie Petheridge?** Winnie is a key member of Shirley's team leading a rebellion against Conrad's rule.

**Where have I seen Sam Lawton before?** Lawton has previously had roles in [Silent Witness](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/silent-witness-season-29-release-date/) and You Don't Know Me.

**Ruth Madeley plays Shirley Anne Bingham**
-------------------------------------------

![Image 8: Ruth Madeley as Shirley in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521370-e4fa772.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ruth Madeley as Shirley in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Samuel Dore

**Who is Shirley Anne Bingham?** Shirley is UNIT's scientific advisor. In Wish World, she was seen leading a rebellion against the tyrannical Conrad.

**Where have I seen Ruth Madeley before?** Madeley has had roles in series including Fresh Meat, [Outnumbered](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/outnumbered-2024-christmas-special-cast/), Cold Feet, Years and Years, The Long Shadow, [Brassic](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/brassic-season-7-sky-release-date/), [Renegade Nell](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/fantasy/renegade-nell-season-2-release/) and [Nightsleeper](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/nightsleeper-season-2-release-date/), as well as films such as [Joy](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/james-norton-big-rt-interview-joy-netflix/) and the TV movie Then Barbara Met Alan.

**Michelle Greenidge plays Carla Sunday**
-----------------------------------------

![Image 9: Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2023/12/457020-2d0803c.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday in Doctor Who. BBC Studios

**Who is Carla Sunday?** Carla is Ruby's adoptive mother.

**Where have I seen Michelle Greenidge before?** Greenidge has previously had roles in series such as It's a Sin, After Life, Mandy, Code 404, The Witchfinder, Alex Rider, Grantchester, Small Axe, [KAOS](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/fantasy/kaos-netflix-season-2-release/) and [Death in Paradise](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-season-15-release-date/). She has also had roles in films including Cruella and [Venom: Let There Be Carnage](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/venom-3-release-date-trailer-story/).

**Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps plays Poppy**
-------------------------------------------

![Image 10: Varada Sethu as Belinda and Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521373-0b941e4.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda and Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Poppy?** Poppy was one of the babies abandoned on Baby Station Beta that the Doctor and Ruby met in Space Babies. At the end of that episode, she and her crew flew to a new planet, but she was recently seen as an apparition, appearing to Belinda in Lagos, Nigeria, in The Story and the Engine. In Conrad’s wish world, Poppy was reimagined as the daughter of Belinda and ‘John Smith’ (aka the Doctor).

**Where have I seen** **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps** **before?** Doctor Who is young actor Mavanga-Phipps's only credit thus far.

**Jemma Redgrave plays Kate Lethbridge-Stewart**
------------------------------------------------

![Image 11: Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge Stewart and Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/518799-bd774f9.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge Stewart and Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Kate Lethbridge-Stewart?** Kate is an old friend of the Doctor and the daughter of the Brigadier, who now runs UNIT. In Wish World, Kate was transformed into the leader of the “Unified National Insurance Team”.

**Where have I seen Jemma Redgrave before?** As well as her role in Doctor Who, Redgrave is also known for appearing in series such as Bramwell, Holby City, [Grantchester](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/grantchester-season-10-release-date/) and Silent Witness, as well as films including Howards End, Red, White & Royal Blue and The Beekeeper.

**Susan Twist plays Susan Triad**
---------------------------------

![Image 12: Susan Twist as Susan Triad in Doctor Who, stood at a computer](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521379-1a97496.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Susan Twist as Susan Triad in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is Susan Triad?** Susan Triad was previously an angel of death created by Sutekh, who was planted across the universe and timeline wherever the TARDIS landed. One version of her became a tech mogul in 21st century Britain, founding Triad Technology. When Sutekh was defeated, this version of her became a normal human, and was offered a job at UNIT.

**Where have I seen Susan Twist before?** Twist has been seen in Coronation Street and In the Flesh.

**Alexander Devrient plays Colonel Christopher Ibrahim**
--------------------------------------------------------

![Image 13: Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521376-229dc38.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Colonel Christopher Ibrahim?** Colonel Ibrahim is a key soldier at UNIT. Like his comrades, Ibrahim worked at the “Unified National Insurance Team” in Conrad’s wish world.

**Where have I seen Alexander Devrient before?** Devrient has had roles in films such as Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows and The Danish Girl, as well as series including [Emmerdale](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/emmerdale/), [Industry](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/industry-season-4-release-date/), [Motherland](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/amandaland-review/), [Ted Lasso](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/ted-lasso-season-4-release-date/) and [The Lazarus Project](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/anjli-mohindra-the-lazarus-project-cancellation-gutted-exclusive-newsupdate/).

**Aidan Cook plays The Vlinx**
------------------------------

![Image 14: The Vlinx in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521377-80a8e12.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

The Vlinx in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is The Vlinx?** The Vlinx a robotic being who works for UNIT, and was first seen in 60th anniversary special The Giggle.

**Where have I seen Aidan Cook before?** As well as playing multiple costumed characters in Doctor Who, Cook has had roles in Fimbles, ZingZillas, Horrid Henry, multiple Star Wars projects and Willow.

**Yasmin Finney** **plays** **Rose Noble**
------------------------------------------

![Image 15: Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble in Doctor Who's The Legend of Ruby Sunday](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/06/480146-3284954.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble in Doctor Who's The Legend of Ruby Sunday. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Rose Noble?** Rose is the daughter of the Doctor's former companion, Donna Noble. She was last seen working at UNIT in Empire of Death.

**Where have I seen Yasmin Finney before?** As well as her role as Rose in Doctor Who, Finney is best known for playing Elle in Netflix's [Heartstopper](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/heartstopper-season-4-release-date/).

**Bonnie Langford plays Melanie Bush**
--------------------------------------

![Image 16: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor and Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520875-0d6ab81.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor and Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Melanie Bush**? Mel is a companion who first travelled with the Sixth and Seventh Doctors in the classic run of Doctor Who. She returned as a staff member at UNIT in the 60th anniversary specials. In Conrad’s wish world, Melanie was cast as Belinda and John’s neighbour.

**Where have I seen Bonnie Langford before?** Aside from Doctor Who, Langford is known as a theatre icon, and starred as Carmel Kazemi in EastEnders from 2015 to 2018.

**Angela Wynter plays Cherry Sunday**
-------------------------------------

![Image 17: Cherry (Angela Wynter) in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2023/12/457037-b061636.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Cherry (Angela Wynter) in Doctor Who. Lara Cornell/Bad Wolf/BBC Studios 2023

**Who is Cherry Sunday?** Cherry is Carla's mother and therefore Ruby's grandmother.

**Where have I seen Angela Wynter before?** Wynter is best known for playing Yolande in EastEnders, while she has also had roles in series such as Holby City, Cleaning Up, Doctors, Mood, This England, Vampire Academy, [Call the Midwife](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/call-the-midwife-season-15-release-date/), Three Little Birds and Time.

**[Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) continues on Saturday 31st May at 6:50pm on BBC One and BBC iPlayer in the UK. The series is available on Disney+ outside of the UK.**

By

[Peter Nolan](https://www.blogtorwho.com/author/peter/)

\-

09/06/2025

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.blogtorwho.com%2Fdoctor-who-viewing-figures-the-reality-war-7%2F "Facebook")[Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Doctor+Who+Viewing+Figures%3A+The+Reality+War+%2B7&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.blogtorwho.com%2Fdoctor-who-viewing-figures-the-reality-war-7%2F&via=BlogtorWho "Twitter")[Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.blogtorwho.com/doctor-who-viewing-figures-the-reality-war-7/&media=https://www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/521376-scaled.jpg&description=TheRealityWarfinishesthisseasonofDoctorWhojustinsidetheTop20withoneofhighestdramaviewingfiguresoftheweek "Pinterest")[WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Doctor+Who+Viewing+Figures%3A+The+Reality+War+%2B7%0A%0Ahttps://www.blogtorwho.com/doctor-who-viewing-figures-the-reality-war-7/ "WhatsApp")

[](https://www.blogtorwho.com/doctor-who-viewing-figures-the-reality-war-7/# "More")

 

_The Reality War_ finishes the season just inside the Top 20 as one of the week’s highest rated dramas
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The +7 viewing figure for **Doctor Who’s** 2025 finale are now available. **_The Reality War_ has a +7 rating of 3.44m viewers.** That’s a 58.5% increase on the original official overnight number of 2.17m. However, we still don’t have the pre-transmission iPlayer number. This means we can’t say how much of that 1.27m increase is time-shifting.

 

It’s also an increase of 0.58m (20.3%) on the +7 result for the first half of the finale, _Wish World_. Meanwhile, in our regular year-on-year comparison, it’s a very similar result to last year’s finale. _The Reality War’s_ 3.44m is down just 0.25m (6.8%) on 2024’s _Empire of Death_.

Meanwhile, _The Reality War_ is currently at #18 in the weekly chart. That’s up 12 places from _Wish World_ and exactly the same placement as last year’s finale. It was the **BBC’s** seventh most watched show of the week, and the UK’s second highest rated drama, behind _Death Valley_.

It’s worth noting, though, that last season **Doctor Who** episodes moved up an average of 4 places between the +7 and +28 charts. This year, _The Robot Revolution_ actually climbed 10 places between the initial and final charts. So we can probably expect _The Reality War_ to move at least a few positions in the final results.

[![Image 2: The Doctor (NCUTI GATWA), Belinda (VARADA SETHU) & Ruby Sunday (MILLIE GIBSON), in The Reality War:,COPYRIGHT:BBC Studios,CREDIT LINE:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon. The Doctor and Belinda look at Ruby confused in the UNIT HQ](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/525177-scaled.jpg?resize=696%2C464&quality=89)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/525177-scaled.jpg?quality=89)

The Doctor (NCUTI GATWA), Belinda (VARADA SETHU) & Ruby Sunday (MILLIE GIBSON), in The Reality War:,COPYRIGHT:BBC Studios,CREDIT LINE:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

### From start to finish, the Gatwa era has had similar audience retention to Peter Capaldi’s, and is just below average overall

Overall, with premiere episode _The Robot Revolution_ scoring a +7 of 3.57m, it means that the 2025 season retained 96.4% of it audience across the eight episodes. Since The Reality War was also Ncuti Gatwa’s final episode as the Doctor, we can also observe that he has an overall end-to-end audience retention of 85.8%.

For context, Christopher Eccleston’s was 63.9%, David Tennant’s 142.3%, Matt Smith’s 103%, Peter Capaldi’s 86.4%, and Jodie Whittaker’s 48.4%. This means Gatwa’s retention is just below the overall average of 88.3%.

However, it won’t be until we get the final official +28 viewing figures for the season that we’ll be able to make more definitive conclusions.

Speaking of which, **Blogtor Who** hasn’t seen the +28 rating for _Lux_ yet, though it may be available soon.

5.content:
‘The Reality War’ featured a shock regeneration for the Fifteenth Doctor, marking a true first in the history of _Doctor Who_.

![Image 1: reality war](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/reality-war-ncuti-gatwa-fifteenth-doctor-who-regeneration.jpg)

(C) BBC

For the first time ever in _[Doctor Who](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/category/doctor-who/)_, the lead actor departed without a prior announcement. Normally, when a Doctor regenerates, the public is told many months in advance, and their successor is announced. But in ‘The Reality War,’ the BBC decided to shake things up, and the public was treated to a surprise regeneration. In the episode’s closing moments, the Doctor sacrificed himself to save a child, and miraculously transformed into… well, we’ll come to that.

Of course, there is also the Internet, and rumours had been circulating about Ncuti Gatwa’s regeneration prior to ‘The Reality War’s transmission. But this is the Internet: it also predicted that ‘[Marco Polo](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/missing-doctor-who-episodes-marco-polo/)‘ would be returned in 2013, and we’re still waiting. We have to take things with a pinch of salt.

In addition, in the build-up to ‘The Reality War,’ it had been rather difficult to pin down what, exactly, _Doctor Who_‘s future looked like. A third series had been rumoured, but [Russell T Davies](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-every-russell-t-davies-episode/) made it clear that no announcement about Series Three would be made until after Series Two had aired. The same was true of Disney’s future involvement; nothing was being said. Ncuti Gatwa was remaining tight-lipped. In theory, the second series of this iteration of _Doctor Who_ could have ended and simply not been recommissioned.

In short, most people went into ‘The Reality War’ knowing that all bets were off. But whether they were quite prepared for the surprise appearance of Billie Piper is another story. Because, in the final moments, Ncuti Gatwa’s face faded away to reveal that of his former companion [Rose Tyler](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-companions-rose-tyler/), who looked down the lens and said, with a grin, “Oh, hello!”

So did this mean that Billie Piper was the Sixteenth Doctor? Well, even that wasn’t made clear. In the aftermath of ‘The Reality War,’ all concerned were very careful with their words. This is what Russell T Davies had to say: “Billie once changed the whole of television, back in 2005, and now she’s done it again! It’s an honour and a hoot to welcome her back to the TARDIS, but quite how and why and who is a story yet to be told. After 62 years, the Doctor’s adventures are only just beginning!”

This was followed by a statement from Billie Piper: “It’s no secret how much I love this show, and I have always said I would love to return to the Whoniverse as I have some of my best memories there, so to be given the opportunity to step back on that [TARDIS](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-the-top-5-tardis-stories/) one more time was just something I couldn’t refuse, but who, how, why and when, you’ll just have to wait and see.”

![Image 2: reality war](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/doctor-who-regeneration-reality-war-billie-piper.jpg)

(C) BBC

Eagle-eyed viewers also observed that she wasn’t actually credited as the Doctor at the end of ‘The Reality War.’ The credits simply said, “And introducing Billie Piper.” This could be because she is actually playing some mysterious, alternate character, such as the Moment from ‘[The Day of the Doctor](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/looking-back-on-doctor-whos-50th-anniversary/),’ (the Moment took the face of Rose Tyler, after all.) The more cynical explanation would be that she couldn’t contractually be announced as the Doctor if there was no guarantee that the series would be returning. And at the time of writing, we simply don’t know.

As such, the Fifteenth Doctor’s regeneration at the end of ‘The Reality War’ is one of the most mysterious and unexpected in the series’ history. Certainly, there have been surprise regenerations in the past (like the Tenth Doctor’s in ‘[The Stolen Earth](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/david-tennants-first-doctor-who-episode/)‘ and the War Doctor’s in ‘The Day of the Doctor’) but ‘The Reality War’ takes it to a whole new level, and it’s a testament to the production team that they managed to keep the whole thing largely under wraps before transmission.

But was ‘The Reality War’ a good send-off for the Fifteenth Doctor? It was certainly epic in scale given its run time of 66 minutes, making it one of the [longest _Doctor Who_ episodes ever](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/are-these-the-longest-doctor-who-stories/). And it was rammed: there were two versions of the [Rani](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-villains-who-is-the-rani/), the ancient Time Lord [Omega](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-who-is-omega/), UNIT, two former companions (Ruby and [Mel](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-companions-melanie-bush/)) and even a daughter for the Doctor.

In fact, had it not been for this daughter, the Fifteenth Doctor might have survived. She was a product of the dream world created by Conrad (from ‘[Lucky Day](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/pete-mctighe-cancel-culture-lucky-day/)‘) and the two Ranis, and so when reality returned to normal, she ceased to exist. The Doctor therefore had to sacrifice himself and pour his regeneration energy into the heart of the TARDIS to break the current form of reality and haul his daughter back into existence. Only in _[Doctor Who](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/category/doctor-who/)_, right?

But as he was regenerating, viewers were treated to another surprise in the form of Jodie Whittaker, who made a re-appearance as the Thirteenth Doctor. It’s not entirely clear why her Doctor showed up in the TARDIS during ‘The Reality War,’ but it was a nice surprise for fans of her incarnation.

![Image 3: reality war](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/doctor-who-reality-war-ncuti-gatwa-jodie-whittaker.jpg)

(C) BBC

A more puzzling surprise was the lack of [Susan Foreman](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-what-happened-to-susan-foreman/), who had been teased in the build-up to the finale. She appeared briefly in ‘[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/doctor-who-the-interstellar-song-contest/)‘ and ‘[Wish World](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/wish-world-alternate-reality-doctor-who/),’ so many fans were expecting her to make some sort of appearance in ‘The Reality War.’ After all, she had been interviewed wearing a distinctly futuristic-looking outfit in _Doctor Who Unleashed._

Indeed, the Internet continues to abound with rumours that there is, in fact, a secret alternate ending to ‘The Reality War’ that has now been consigned to the same vault as Eric Stoltz’s _Back to the Future_, and the original cut of _The Shining_. Was Susan originally meant to appear in ‘The Reality War’? Are some unreleased Susan Foreman scenes sitting in the Black Archive? Did the episode originally end without a regeneration? We may never know.

So tell us, reader: where do you think _[Doctor Who](https://blog.lovarzi.co.uk/category/doctor-who/)_ will go next? And is Billie Piper really the Sixteenth Doctor? Let us know in the comments below.
